newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures end mixed despite firm cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures end mixed despite firm cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished mixed Friday despite steady to higher physical prices in the western U.S., stablizing after a recent slide tied to cooler weather, brokers and traders said.
"Futures may be a little undervalued. There was too much selling pressure coming from September (expiring on Tuesday)," said a Houston trader.

The Palo Verde (PV) half of the complex was bolstered by firmer spot electricity and western natural gas prices, while California-Oregon Border (COB) values were tempered by outlook of moderate weather in the Northwest next week, traders said.
October COB futures settled down five cents at $15.70 per megawatt hour (MWh) after reaching as high as $15.85.
November COB fell 15 cents to $16.40. Most deferred months finished lower.
October PV futures ended up 15 cents at $16.45 per MWh after falling as low as $16.20.
November PV rose 20 cents to $15.40. Most PV outer-month contracts settled higher.
NYMEX estimated 209 COB and 32 PV contracts were sold Friday.
NYMEX will be closed Monday in observance of the three-day U.S. Labor Day weekend.
